plan: [With three symmetric bidders and independent uniform values, the Bayes–Nash equilibrium bid is (n-1)/n * v = 2/3 * v. For v = 31 this gives 20.666..., so I round to the nearest $0.1 and bid $20.7 to maximize expected surplus.]

[With 3 bidders and independent uniform values, the symmetric risk-neutral first-price equilibrium bid is (n-1)/n * v = 2/3 * v. No prior rounds to learn from, so follow the equilibrium to maximize long-run profit. For v = 31, 2/3 * 31 = 20.666..., round to the nearest $0.1. Ties are random, so use the equilibrium rounded bid to balance winning probability and payment.]

[Three bidders; first-price sealed-bid. With independent private values, symmetric BNE: b(v)=(n-1)/n v = 2/3 v. For v=46, equilibrium bid ≈30.667.
